content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm currently planning to connect two [product_name] modules via Ethernet. If I want to output a digital signal from the master device and transmit it to the slave, what is the address for the network digital input on the slave device? Could it be NI1? I appreciate any assistance. Regards, [user_name].

[user_name], You'll need to assign different IP addresses to the master and the slave. Then, you can right-click the network input and enter the IP address of the slave unit. I'm traveling at the moment, so I'll assist further when I return. [user_name]

Thank you for your help. I've managed to download the latest [product_name] manual and discovered that the slave [product_name] functions as an additional IN/OUT module with a different designation (NIx and NQx). My question now is, how many slave [product_name] modules can be connected to a single master unit? Regards, [user_name].

A [product_name] operating in slave mode can also use its own expansion modules. It supports up to 24 digital inputs, 8 analog inputs, 16 digital outputs, and 2 analog outputs. Best regards, [user_name]
One final question—if we have one [product_name] as the master and two as slaves, how does the master differentiate I/Os from the first slave versus the second? Regards, [user_name].
[user_name], Each module has its own IP address. This allows you to identify which [product_name] the I/Os are coming from. Hope this clarifies.
Hi, The IP address of each slave module uniquely identifies the units.
New question split: What is the maximum number of digital and/or analog inputs and outputs that can be configured with a master or slave [product_name]?
New question split: How do you set up the mapping (local VB0, remote IB0) between two [product_name] modules?

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are discussing how to configure network communication among several [product_name] modules over Ethernet. The main points of clarification involve the correct addressing of network digital inputs and outputs, distinguishing I/O signals from multiple linked slave units, scalability of the system, and proper mapping of input and output signals across the networked modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect simple network setup for linking [product_name] modules, explicit guidance on network I/O addressing, and clear information regarding system expansion with multiple slave devices.
